stem: A grower sees a mix of clear, cloudy and amber glandular trichomes on different bracts of the same inflorescence. Which interpretation is best supported by current evidence?
choices: Trichome development can be asynchronous and genotype- and age-dependent, so maturity should be interpreted from multiple observations rather than a single color percentage rule
Every trichome on an inflorescence matures at exactly the same time
Amber color alone provides a universal harvest date for every genotype and environment
Trichome appearance is unrelated to plant age
rationale: Research shows asynchronous trichome development and genotype- and age-related variation, so single universal color thresholds should not be treated as definitive harvest rules.
